Class TextEditing

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.tui.event.TextEditing
public final class TextEditing extends Object
Applies key and paste events to a TextInputState or a TextAreaState, the way the toolkit's text inputs and text areas edit them.

In a TuiRunner app, pass the events a focused field should get, after checking the keys the app handles itself, such as Enter to submit: 

if (event instanceof KeyEvent && ((KeyEvent) event).isConfirm()) {
    submit(name.text());
    return true;
}
return TextEditing.handle(name, event);
  • A typed character, a KeyCode.CHAR event without Ctrl or Alt, is inserted whole, also when it is outside the Basic Multilingual Plane. It is inserted even when the bindings bind it to an action, as vim binds h and x: in a text field, letters are text. A character sequence such as a ZWJ emoji arrives as one event per code point, and builds up in the text one code point at a time.
  • Ctrl and Alt characters are never inserted. They edit when the event's bindings bind them to an editing action, such as the emacs Ctrl+B, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+H and Ctrl+D. Otherwise they are left to the app.
  • Actions.MOVE_LEFT and Actions.MOVE_RIGHT move the cursor by one grapheme cluster, Actions.DELETE_BACKWARD and Actions.DELETE_FORWARD delete one, and Actions.HOME and Actions.END move to the start and end. The Left, Right, Backspace, Delete, Home and End keys always do these, with or without modifiers.
  • A PasteEvent is inserted at the cursor.
Each method returns whether the event was handled, which a TuiRunner event handler can return to redraw.

  • Method Details

    • handle

      public static boolean handle(TextInputState state, Event event)
      Applies a key or paste event to a single-line text input.

      A paste is inserted on one line: its line breaks (CRLF, CR or LF) become spaces, and a line break at its start or end is dropped. Other keys, such as Enter, Tab, Escape or Up, are not handled.

      Parameters:
      state - the text input state to edit
      event - the event to apply
      Returns:
      true if the event was handled

    • handle

      public static boolean handle(TextInputState state, Event event, IntPredicate allowed)
      Applies a key or paste event to a single-line text input, inserting only the characters allowed accepts, for example Character::isDigit for a number.

      A typed character that allowed rejects is still handled, without being inserted, so it does not reach the app's own keys while the field has the focus. A paste is filtered by grapheme cluster: a cluster is inserted only when allowed accepts all its code points. Otherwise this works as handle(TextInputState, Event).

      Parameters:
      state - the text input state to edit
      event - the event to apply
      allowed - the code points that may be inserted, or null to insert any
      Returns:
      true if the event was handled

      event - the event to apply

      true if the event was handled

    • handle

      public static boolean handle(TextAreaState state, Event event, Overflow overflow)
      Applies a key or paste event to a multi-line text area.

      Besides the editing described for this class, Enter inserts a line break, Actions.MOVE_UP and Actions.MOVE_DOWN (and the Up and Down keys) move the cursor one row, and Actions.HOME and Actions.END move to the start and end of the line. With a wrapping overflow, Up and Down move by the rows on screen, at the width of the text area's last render. A paste keeps its line breaks, with CRLF and CR turned into LF. Tab is not handled, as it moves the focus in the bindings.

      Parameters:
      state - the text area state to edit
      event - the event to apply
      overflow - the overflow the text area is rendered with, as given to TextArea.Builder.overflow; null is Overflow.CLIP
      Returns:
      true if the event was handled
